ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle OCD$ share a common vertex $O$, and $\triangle OAB \cong \triangle OCD$. As shown in Figure 1, $O$ is a point on side $BC$. Given that $AO=DO$, and if $\angle AOD=80^\circ$, connect $AC$ and $BD$, with the intersection point being $E$. Find the measure of $\angle DEC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown, \\
$\because$ $\triangle OAB \cong \triangle OCD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BOA = \angle COD = \frac{180^\circ - 80^\circ}{2} = 50^\circ, OA = OC, OB = OD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOC = \angle DOB = 130^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACO = \angle DBO = \frac{180^\circ - 130^\circ}{2} = 25^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle DEC = \boxed{50^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure gives two schematic diagrams, among which Figure 1 is the configuration used in this problem. In Figure 1, B, O, C are on the same horizontal straight line, and O is between B and C; A and D are both above the straight line BC; segment OA points from O to A in the upper left, and segment OD points from O to D in the upper right, therefore the straight angle from ray OB to ray OC is divided by OA and OD into three parts: ∠BOA, ∠AOD, and ∠DOC. The figure also shows sides such as AB, AD, and DC, and the problem asks to further connect AC and BD, intersecting at E. Then reason: From the meaning of the problem, △OAB ≅ △OCD, and according to the correspondence, ∠BOA = ∠COD can be obtained, and OA = OC, OB = OD. Because B, O, C are collinear, ∠BOA + ∠AOD + ∠DOC = 180°. It is known that ∠AOD = 80°, and also ∠BOA = ∠DOC, so ∠BOA = ∠DOC = (180° - 80°) / 2 = 50°. Thus ∠AOC = ∠AOD + ∠DOC = 80° + 50° = 130°; similarly, ∠DOB = ∠DOA + ∠AOB = 80° + 50° = 130°. In △AOC, OA = OC, so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angle ∠ACO = (180° - 130°) / 2 = 25°. In △DBO, DO = OB, so it is also an isosceles triangle, and the base angle ∠DBO = (180° - 130°) / 2 = 25°. Since BO and CO are opposite rays on the same straight line, AC is inclined 25° to one side relative to the baseline, and BD is inclined 25° to the other side relative to the baseline. E is the intersection point of AC and BD, so ∠DEC is the included angle formed by these two straight lines at E, and its measure is 25° + 25° = 50°.
